cards.text: Four trumpets have sounded, and an eagle has cried woe three times over the trumpets still to come (Revelation 8:7-13). Now the fifth angel sounds his trumpet. John, the one seeing this vision (Revelation 1:9), sees a star that had fallen from heaven to earth.

cards.question: The fallen star in John's vision is given something. What is it?

answers.text: The key to the pit of the Abyss
A golden censer full of incense
A sharp sickle for the harvest

cards.text: The star opens the pit, and smoke rises out of it like the smoke of a great furnace. I've set off a smoke alarm or two in my bakery, friend, but never like THIS.

cards.question: The smoke rising from the pit of the Abyss darkens the sun and the air.

cards.text: Then out of the smoke, locusts descend on the earth, and they're given power like that of the scorpions of the earth. Friend, I lose my MIND when one fly gets into my bakery.

cards.question: Locusts usually go straight for anything green. These locusts are told they may harm the grass, plants and trees.
The locusts in John's vision are told who they may harm. Who is it?

answers.text: Only those without God's seal on their foreheads
Only the kings and the mighty of the earth
Only the people who live along the sea

cards.question: The locusts from the Abyss are given power to kill the people without God's seal.

cards.text: They can only torment those people for five months, and the torment is like the stinging of a scorpion. I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: The locusts can torment people but not kill them. So John says that in those days, people will long to ___, but it will escape them.

cards.text: Then John describes these locusts, so hold on to your apron, friend. They have something like crowns of gold on their heads, and their faces are like the faces of men.

cards.question: John says the locusts in his vision look like horses. What kind of horses?

cards.text: Their hair is like that of women, and their teeth are like those of lions.

cards.question: The locusts in John's vision have breastplates like breastplates of iron, and their wings sound like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.

cards.text: To top it off, they have tails with stingers like scorpions, with power to injure people for five months. Crowns, armor AND scorpion tails, and I thought my chef's hat was a lot.

cards.question: The locusts in John's vision aren't on their own. They have a king ruling over them. Who is he?

cards.text: His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek it is Apollyon. I've got two names too, friend, but nobody ever trembled at Papa or Dorin.

cards.question: The eagle cried woe three times. Now the first woe has passed, and ___ woes are still to follow.

cards.text: Then the sixth angel sounds his trumpet, and John hears a voice speaking to that very angel.

cards.question: When the sixth angel sounds his trumpet, the voice John hears comes from the four horns of the golden ___.

cards.text: The voice tells the sixth angel, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."
These four angels had been prepared for this hour and day and month and year. Friend, I set three alarms and STILL hit snooze, and these angels were ready down to the HOUR.

cards.question: The four angels from the Euphrates are released. What are they released to do?

answers.text: Gather the harvest of the earth

cards.text: Then comes the number of mounted troops: two hundred million. Two hundred MILLION, and I lose count of my cookie trays after nine.

cards.question: John says he heard the number of the mounted troops.
The riders in John's vision have breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire and sulfur. What are the horses' heads like?

cards.text: Out of the horses' mouths come fire, smoke and sulfur. Those three plagues kill a third of mankind.
The power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails. The locusts had stingers on their tails, but these tails are something else.

cards.question: The horses' tails in John's vision are like ___, having heads with which to inflict harm.
The rest of mankind lives through these plagues, and they keep worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood. What does John say about those idols?

answers.text: They cannot see or hear or walk
They were carried off to Babylon
They were broken in the earthquake

cards.question: The survivors in John's vision turn away from their murder, sorcery, sexual immorality and theft.

cards.text: And that's where we'll stop for now, friend. Keep your apron on, because this story is NOT done.
